definition: A middle path storing one vector per token and computing fine-grained token-level matching (MaxSim) at query time.
details: A middle path storing one vector per token and computing fine-grained token-level matching (MaxSim) at query time. More accurate than single-vector retrieval, cheaper than cross-encoders, at the cost of much larger indexes.

explainer.lead: Late Interaction keeps one vector per token and compares query and document tokens only at search time, sitting between single-vector and cross-encoder retrieval. It matters because it buys token-level accuracy without the per-query cost of a cross-encoder.

tiers.eli5: Instead of summarising a whole page in one fingerprint, you keep a fingerprint for every word and check them word by word when someone asks. It is more careful than one-fingerprint matching but takes much more shelf space.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers store per-token vectors in the index and score with MaxSim at query time, getting better ranking than single-vector search at lower query cost than a cross-encoder. The pitfall is index size: storing a vector per token makes the index far larger.
tiers.paperLevel: Each query and document is represented as a set of token vectors; the score is MaxSim, the sum over query tokens of the maximum similarity to any document token. The known limit is a much larger index than single-vector retrieval.

explainer.example: A query of five tokens is scored against a document by, for each query token, taking its best match among the document's token vectors and summing those five maxima.
